claims.statement: For every m>=1 and every p satisfying x(T_m)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T_m)+1, the complete ordinary favorable-leaf sum S(T_m,p) is strictly negative.
claims.scope: Only the ordinary trees T_m consisting of path a-b-r with m centers adjacent to r, each center having three private leaves; original leaves and the fixed strict selector are used. The result depends on the admitted finite-forest strict-descent bound n<=4x and an exact finite Python base for m=3..999 with algebraic estimates for m>=1000. It makes no assertion for arbitrary trees.
claims.reason: retained — independent audit found the polynomial and support-deletion identities consistent, verified that the same fixed strict selector covers the two original-leaf orbits throughout the eligible rank window, checked the tagged global sum identity, and reproduced the exact finite replay with zero failures. The analytic tail argument supplies the remaining all-m inequalities. Evidence supports only this computer-assisted family theorem; it does not prove the all-tree primary.

limitations: The claim is restricted to the specified T_m family and does not settle the arbitrary-tree lower-region aggregate.
The finite base is exact Python arithmetic and is not Lean/kernel checked.
The all-m selector bridge depends on the admitted R27 forest strict-descent bound n<=4x; this critique does not reprove that theorem.
The proof imports Gurvits Theorem 1.1 for convolution of finite-order ULC sequences; its hypotheses and factor-order application are stated in the report.
